'''Takehime Shrine''' (たけひめじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located along the {{ill|Moto-Arakawa River|Q11388047|qid=Q11388047}} in {{ill|Okegawa, Saitama|Q570333|qid=Q570333}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. The enshrined deity is Toyotake-hime no Mikoto. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=minor shrine listed in the Engishiki}} of {{ill|Adachi district|Q11637033|qid=Q11637033}}, {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== History ===
It is said to have been founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Annei|Q313345|qid=Q313345}} (567 BCE – 510 BCE). In the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} (1868), the shrine’s name was changed from “Himemiya Shrine” to “Takehime Shrine.” With the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, the monk of its affiliated temple, Kongō-ji, returned to secular life and became a Shinto priest, managing the shrine until 1887 (Meiji 20). In 1873 (Meiji 6), it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}, and in 1887 (Meiji 20), the priesthood was transferred from the Kaneda family to the Sakurai family of Kanō. In 1907 (Meiji 40), the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari Shrine}} located at Ōaza Gochōdai, Aza Kamikōchi, was enshrined together with it.

=== Enshrined deities ===
In the place name Shinotsu where the shrine stands, “shino” refers to bamboo and “tsu” means a landing place; in the past, there was a large marsh called Shinotsu-numa here. As the area was surrounded by farmland, it is said that a goddess who personified rice was enshrined.
* {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotake-hime no Mikoto}} (とよあしたけひめのみこと)
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama no Mikoto}} (うかのみたまのみこと) 

=== Festivals ===
* Kinensai (February 11)
* Annual Grand Festival (March 15)
* Fusegi (April 1)
* Niinamesai (November 13)

=== Sub-shrines ===
The various shrines of Shinotsu that had been worshiped separately in three districts are enshrined together.

* Inari Shrine
* Mitsumine Shrine

=== Access ===
* From the east exit of {{ill|Okegawa Station|Q844901|qid=Q844901}} on the JR East {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}}, take the Asahi Bus bound for “Shōbu Shako” for 20 minutes
* Get off at the “Tōbu Industrial Park Entrance” bus stop, then walk 5 minutes
